prompt:
Write 12 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim, in time order. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1059; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: The claimant reported a low-speed head-on collision and stated that the vehicle was struck while travelling in a single lane. The claimant is not represented by counsel and was asked to provide a written account.

Entry 2: Police attendance is confirmed and the responding officer recorded the claimant as the driver of the vehicle at the scene. The report is on file.

Entry 3: Witness statements were obtained from two bystanders who describe the impact exactly as the claimant did. Both witnesses are willing to be contacted again if needed.

Entry 4: Photographs of the vehicle show front-end damage that is consistent with the reported impact. The pattern and location of the damage line up with a head-on contact.

Entry 5: The other driver's account matches the claimant's description of how the collision occurred. No conflict has been identified between the two statements.

Entry 6: The claimant described the same sequence of events in the first call, the recorded statement and the follow-up interview. Details were consistent throughout.

Entry 7: The claimant reports neck and back strain and states that symptoms began shortly after the collision. The reported injuries are the type typically associated with a collision of this force.

Entry 8: Medical records show the claimant attended treatment at a usual pace, with care tapering as symptoms improved. No unusual gaps or escalations appear in the file.

Entry 9: Prior records were checked and no earlier injury to the neck or back has been found. The claimant also confirmed no previous complaints in that area.

Entry 10: Vehicle history was reviewed and no earlier damage to the vehicle has been identified. Nothing in the records suggests the damage predates the policy period.

Entry 11: The driver is listed as a named driver on the policy, and the coverage was in force on the date of loss. Nothing has been found to question the policy status.

Entry 12: Based on the photos, witness accounts, police report and medical file, the claim is progressing as a standard low-speed collision with a routine injury course. File is being prepared for settlement review.
